To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
longitudinal metatranscripts of a meat spoilages microbiome can be used to detect the onset of sensory spoilage.
the longitudinal behavior of beef spoilage microbiome can be described using the functional gene annotations and that the expression of the stress response genes is connected to the spoilage.

the active genes of the spoilage microbiome of a MAP beef product were related to the fermentation of carbohydrates and the management of environmental stress during shelf life and the following storage period.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the active microbial community in food and the genes that are transcribed during the course of time in a food system.
the longitudinal behavior of an active microbiome during meat spoilage and the identification of RNA-based markers for sensory defects.
the longitudinal behavior of the actively transcribed microbial community during shelf life and the development of sensory deterioration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our study showed that the active microbiome of the beef product changed over the time, and these changes were related to the development of sensory defects.
the active genes and pathways of the SSO are the best indicators of the sensory quality of foods.
the longitudinal behavior of the microbiome in the MAP beef product is characterized by continued fermentation and stress responses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to identify the key genes and pathways that are connected with the spoilage of the MAP beef product during shelf life and even onward.
during meat spoilage, the community continues to ferment and manage environmental stress.
the longitudinal metatranscription analysis of a meat microbiome during shelf-life and beyond revealed that the active microbiome was characterized by a core community of lactic acid bacteria.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the active microbiome is a better predictor of quality deterioration than the total microbiome.
the longitudinal metatranscriptional approach provides new information about the spoilage microbiome that is important to develop new tools for food quality analysis.
the longitudinal behavior of the active microbiome is more pronounced than the species composition.
